reviews.one_line_contribution: Reframes retrieved-experience memory harm as a procedural failure — the agent stops gathering evidence early because memory hands it an outcome — and tests that reframing with a token-matched outcome-redaction contrast, a content-free evidence floor applied to both memory and memory-free arms as an interaction, and a claim that a GEPA-searched instruction cannot substitute for the floor.
reviews.closest_prior_work: The proposal correctly identifies Xiong et al., arXiv:2505.16067 (experience-following / misaligned experience replay) and concedes the phenomenon to it; that concession is fair and handled honestly, and the mediation framing does survive it. The threats it misses are outside the agent-memory literature and are more damaging to the individual components. First, the 'evidence floor' is attribution-gated answering, which is a solved-and-published RAG design: citation-constrained generation (ALCE-style 'generate text with citations'), Self-RAG's retrieve/critique tokens, and FLARE/IRCoT's retrieve-until-supported control flow all already enforce 'do not answer until your own retrieval supports the answer', and all already report that it reduces unsupported answers. The paper would therefore be claiming a known intervention as its causal instrument; the novelty must live entirely in the memory-by-floor interaction, which the writing does not make clear. Second, and worse for the mediator, MuSiQue (Trivedi et al., 2022) — one of the three pooled datasets — was constructed around a disconnected-reasoning (DiRe) probe that measures exactly whether a system produced the answer without performing the intermediate hops, and Min et al. 2019 ('Compositional questions do not necessitate multi-hop reasoning') established that HotpotQA-distractor is largely answerable by single-hop shortcutting. 'Evidence sufficiency' is a rebadged DiRe, and 'agents in multi-hop QA answer without gathering the evidence' is the baseline state of these benchmarks, not a memory effect. Neither line is cited.
reviews.strongest_objection: The title claim — that instruction optimization cannot repair this — is over-determined by the design rather than tested by it, and the headline interaction is underpowered by the proposal's own arithmetic. (a) On claim (iii): G1's failure is guaranteed by three independent design choices. GEPA is selected on train-split task accuracy, not on floor compliance or trajectory length; on a 150-instance train split with a ~10% break rate there are roughly 15 informative broken episodes to reflect over; and 400 rollouts is a thin search. If memory is net-positive on the train split (the precheck only requires breaks ≥4% and fixes ≥4%), there is no selection pressure toward 'keep looking' at all, so 'G1 recovers <1/3 of the floor's benefit' is a prediction about this GEPA configuration's objective and budget, not about the instruction slot. Worse, the comparison is structurally a hard programmatic constraint versus a politely worded request, and the fact that models comply with enforced constraints more than with instructions is known a priori — it is not a discovery about what prompt optimization can own, and it certainly does not license 'some agent pathologies are not addressable by prompt optimization at all'. The proposal's own mitigation (report the evolved text, report the score trajectory) does not remove the objective mismatch. (b) On power: breaks under M1 are budgeted at ~50/500 = 10 points. Prediction 3 asks for ≥50% break reduction under M1+Fh (≥5 points) with M0+Fh gaining less than a third of that (<1.7 points), so the predicted interaction is ~3.3 points — against a stated interaction MDE of ~6 points. The headline causal test is, by the proposal's own numbers, powered at roughly half the effect it predicts, and this is before the Holm correction across a family of eleven-plus arms, which the α=0.05 MDE calculation does not absorb. If the precheck merely clears its 4% gate, a halving of breaks is a 2-point effect against a 6-point MDE and the central experiment cannot return a result in either direction. (c) A secondary but real problem: the floor is defined as 'the agent may not answer until it has itself retrieved supporting spans', and the mediator is defined as 'do the supporting spans appear in this episode's own retrievals'. The causal instrument is the operational negation of the mediator, so Analysis 2 is close to definitionally true and carries less evidential weight than its billing as 'the causal test' suggests. Similarly, with an ExpeL bank built from the training splits of the same three datasets, a retrieved item for a near-duplicate question will often contain a directly appropriable answer string; predicting memory-echo >40% on wrong answers concedes that the phenomenon may reduce to answer-copying, and M3 ('outcome-only shortcuts maximally') is then near-tautological rather than a mechanism finding.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Four changes, in order of importance. (1) Fix the power on the endpoint that carries the paper: enrich the test set for break-eligible instances using the dev bank and precheck (stratified sampling of instances where memory is retrieved with high similarity), or raise n on the M1/M1+Fh/M0/M0+Fh cells specifically and cut arms elsewhere, and re-derive the interaction MDE under the Holm-corrected alpha. State the interaction MDE conditional on the precheck's observed break rate, not on the optimistic 10% figure. (2) Make (iii) falsifiable in the direction that would refute it: give GEPA a rollout-budget scaling curve (e.g. 400 / 1600 / 6400) so a plateau is evidence rather than an artifact; run at least one second optimizer (MIPRO) so the claim is about instruction search rather than about GEPA; and give one variant an objective that includes evidence sufficiency or compliance, so a failure cannot be attributed to the optimizer never having been asked. Then retitle to what the design supports — something like 'instruction-level repairs underperform a control-flow floor at matched search budget' — rather than 'instruction optimization cannot repair it'. (3) Add the crossed cells the factorial omits: M2+Fh, M3+Fh and G1+Fh. Without G1+Fh the enforcement-versus-discovery story is asserted from the compliance readout alone; without M2+Fh you cannot tell whether redaction and the floor are addressing the same mechanism or are additive, which is the difference between a mechanism paper and two separate interventions. (4) Break the answer-copying confound: add an outcome-mismatched arm (same task family, procedure intact, outcome shuffled from a different instance so it is outcome-bearing but not appropriable). If truncation happens there too, the mechanism is 'an outcome terminates the search'; if it does not, the mechanism is 'memory supplied a usable answer' and the paper is a copying study. Also drop or heavily de-emphasize Analysis 5, whose fingerprint is guaranteed by construction since the bank is built pre-perturbation.
reviews.missing_baseline: Memory-dropout at the answer step: memory injected during planning and tool use, then removed from context before the final-answer turn. This is cheap, content-free, and lives in the control flow like the floor, but it discriminates exactly the hypothesis under test — if removing memory only at termination recovers most of M1+Fh's break reduction, the harm is that memory supplies an answer at commitment time, not that it truncates the search, and the entire premature-termination framing collapses into memory-echo. The plan has no arm that separates these. Two further omissions a reviewer will raise: (a) a runtime memory-gating / selective-injection baseline (inject only when a calibrated signal says the item will help, or inject k adaptively per instance) — this is the track's own open question and it lives in the demonstration slot, which the paper's instruction-versus-control-flow dichotomy silently excludes, so a cheap gate matching the floor would undercut the division-of-labour framing; and (b) the crossed cells G1+Fh, M2+Fh, M3+Fh, and M4+Fh.
reviews.preprint_collision: Above average for this kind of submission and clearly done rather than asserted: it names one specific closest work with an arXiv ID, concedes the phenomenon to it, states the manipulation that distinguishes the two, and gives a condition under which the prior work is complete and this proposal is wrong. That is the right shape. Three problems. First, credibility: the section itself discloses that an earlier draft cited a dozen forward-dated arXiv IDs the author could not verify. That history means the remaining IDs cannot be taken on trust, and every entry except 2505.16067 is a 2026 identifier (2604.27003, 2605.24941, 2607.06595, 2608.02508, 2605.18930) that a reviewer cannot confirm from the submission. The novelty case therefore rests on exactly one verifiable anchor while claiming a clean field around it. Second, the search is scoped entirely to agent-memory keywords and misses the two literatures that actually threaten the components: RAG attribution and adaptive-retrieval work (Self-RAG, FLARE, IRCoT, citation-gated answering) makes the evidence floor a published intervention rather than a new instrument, and multi-hop shortcut work (Min et al. 2019 on HotpotQA; MuSiQue's own disconnected-reasoning probe) makes 'evidence sufficiency' a rebadged existing metric and establishes the base-rate shortcutting the study attributes to memory. Neither is mentioned, so the check's 'explicit gap statement' is narrower than it reads. Third, the honest caveat is correct and load-bearing: no OpenReview sweep was performed, and by the proposal's own admission an outcome-redaction or step-floor ablation plausibly sits in a recent agent-memory appendix. I would not call this a collision, but I would not treat the novelty as established either — it is one verified citation plus a set of unverifiable ones, with the adjacent 2604.27003 conceded as a near-miss on the paper's own key content contrast.

reviews.one_line_contribution: That the harm from retrieved-experience memory in a ReAct agent is mediated by premature termination of evidence gathering — outcome-bearing items shorten the search — such that a content-free, programmatically enforced evidence floor repairs it while a GEPA-searched instruction cannot.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two threats. (a) Xiong et al., arXiv:2505.16067, which the proposal correctly identifies and correctly does not try to re-own; after crediting it, the residual novelty is a mediator variable and an intervention, not a phenomenon. (b) The one the proposal never mentions and that I think is more damaging: the RAG knowledge-conflict / context-over-reliance literature. The finding that a model presented with a plausible answer in its context adopts it and stops reasoning, that entity-substituted corpora make the model return the context-consistent stale value, and that 'does the supporting evidence appear in the retrieved context' (sufficient-context style labelling) predicts unfaithful answering, are all established there on non-agentic RAG. Analysis 5 is an entity-substitution conflict probe with 'memory' in place of 'retrieved passage'; prediction 2 restates over-reliance; prediction 8 restates the known confidence miscalibration under conflicting context. The proposal's genuine delta over that literature is that the shortcut manifests as *fewer tool calls* rather than as a wrong answer at fixed context — real, but narrower than the abstract claims. arXiv:2604.27003's procedural-beats-trajectory result further pre-empts M2>M3 directionally, as the proposal concedes.
reviews.strongest_objection: Prediction 6 — the headline 'instruction optimization cannot own this' — is close to definitionally true as operationalized, and where it is not definitional it is confounded. M1+Fh is a harness that *rejects* the answer and *forces* up to three additional tool calls; G1 and M1+Fs are text that *asks* for the same behaviour. Any hard constraint beats any soft request in a small open-weight model, on any pathology, with or without memory; a 'GEPA writes verification language and compliance does not move' result is an instruction-following result about Qwen2.5-14B, not a division-of-labour result about memory-induced shortcutting. The confound is concrete and uncontrolled: Fh grants extra call budget beyond the shared step limit, G1 does not, and M6 gives the budget control only to M1 — there is no G1+budget or M1+Fs+budget arm, so part of the floor's advantage over G1 is purchased affordance rather than enforcement-versus-instruction. Second, independent objection: the interaction in Analysis 2 compares floor efficacy on non-comparable error populations. M1's breaks are, by selection, instances M0 already solved — shallow, recoverable errors. M0's errors include genuinely hard multi-hop failures the floor cannot fix at any call budget. So (M1−M1+Fh) > (M0−M0+Fh) is the expected result from error composition and headroom alone, with no memory-specific mechanism. Third, prediction 1 conditions on a collider: break/fix subsets are defined by the M1-vs-M0 outcome, then compared on trajectory length. Episodes that terminate early are more likely to be wrong under M0 too, so 'broken instances have shorter trajectories' is partly guaranteed by the selection rule and is reported with no within-M0 length-vs-correctness null.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Make the repair ladder affordance-matched: run G1 and M1+Fs with the same +3-call allowance the floor consumes, and — the arm that would make (iii) a real claim — give GEPA the *same programmatic hook* the floor uses (optimizer writes the sufficiency criterion, harness enforces it). If optimizer-authored enforcement matches Fh, the claim is 'the instruction slot cannot enforce', which is honest and modest; if it does not, the claim is about search, not about slots. (2) Cross the floor with the content arms (M2+Fh, M3+Fh, M4+Fh). As written the paper has a content half and a control-flow half that never meet; M3+Fh is the single most informative cell, because it asks whether enforcement neutralizes the maximally shortcutting content. (3) Report the M0-only correlation between trajectory length and correctness as the null expectation for prediction 1, and re-derive the mediation against it. (4) Stratify the M0+Fh comparison by matched instance difficulty, or use M4+Fh rather than M0+Fh as the reference for the interaction, so the contrast is between error populations of comparable recoverability. (5) Report GEPA at more than one search seed and more than 400 rollouts, since the load-bearing result is a negative about a stochastic search. (6) Drop or re-power prediction 4's fix-retention threshold: at a 4% precheck floor, 'M2 retains ≥70% of M1's fixes' is a proportion over ~20 instances and cannot be estimated to anything like that resolution.
reviews.missing_baseline: Demonstration-slot optimization. The division-of-labour ladder has exactly two rungs — instruction search (G1) and control flow (Fh) — plus a fixed k=3. The track's own framing puts the memory/demonstration slot in play, and the obvious competitor is optimizing *what gets injected*: MIPRO-style demonstration selection over the frozen bank, or a per-instance calibrated injection budget that admits items only when retrieval-conflict is low. If selecting better items, or admitting fewer of them adaptively, matches the floor's break reduction while keeping fixes, then the repair does belong to a prompt-optimization surface after all and prediction (iii) is refuted by an arm the plan never runs. A reviewer will also demand G1+Fh (are they redundant or additive?) and a late-injection control, where memory is shown only after the agent has gathered evidence, which tests the ordering account of truncation without any enforcement machinery.
reviews.preprint_collision: Better than most: it names a real closest work, states an explicit partial collision on the phenomenon, admits that a prior draft contained a dozen unverifiable forward-dated IDs, and states the ICLR/NeurIPS portal gap. That honesty is credited. But it is still weak as evidence of novelty. No queries, dates, venues, or search surfaces are reported, so the search is unauditable. Having disclosed that an earlier draft fabricated IDs, the section then rests on six IDs (2604.27003, 2605.24941, 2608.02508, 2605.18930, 2512.16962, 2607.06595) that I cannot verify and whose fabrication risk the proposal itself has established; the honest disclosure ironically lowers my confidence in the surviving citations rather than raising it. More substantively, the search is aimed only at agent-memory work and misses the two literatures most likely to contain the result: (a) RAG knowledge-conflict and context-over-reliance, where entity-substituted corpora, context-consistent stale answers, and confidence miscalibration under conflicting evidence are established — Analysis 5 is that paradigm rebadged, and it is cited nowhere; (b) sufficient-context / attribution work in RAG, which supplies the exact evidence-sufficiency label the mediation model depends on; (c) deep-research and search-agent work on under-searching and test-time search-depth scaling, which the proposal waves off as 'early exit as a desired efficiency behaviour' — that is not the same as having searched for papers that force additional retrieval before answering and measure the accuracy gain. I do not believe there is a single preprint making this exact mediated claim about agentic memory, so this is not a fatal collision; but the unsearched neighbouring literature means the novelty on the mechanism is smaller than claimed, and the collision check does not establish otherwise.

reviews.one_line_contribution: That retrieved-experience memory harms agents by making them stop gathering evidence early rather than by supplying bad advice, evidenced by a token-matched outcome-redaction contrast (M2 vs M3) and by a harness-enforced evidence floor (M1+Fh) that a GEPA-searched instruction (G1) allegedly cannot match.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Xiong et al., arXiv:2505.16067 (experience-following / misaligned experience replay), which the proposal correctly identifies and concedes owns the phenomenon; what it leaves open is the mediator, so novelty rests entirely on the three downstream pieces. Two bodies of work the proposal does not engage threaten those pieces harder than 2505.16067 does. (a) The sufficient-context / abstention line (Joren et al., 'Sufficient Context: A New Lens on RAG Systems', ICLR 2025, and its successors) already establishes that LLM agents answer confidently on insufficient context, already operationalizes the exact binary 'evidence sufficiency' instrumented here, and already shows that context-driven premature answering drives error - meaning predictions 2 and 8 are close to re-measurements in a memory wrapper. (b) The citation-grounded generation line (Self-RAG, ALCE-style attribution, verify-before-answer scaffolds) is the evidence floor: 'the agent must list retrieved spans that support the answer before it may emit one, and the harness rejects it otherwise' is an existing technique, not a new intervention, so M1+Fh's novelty is only its use as an interaction probe. arXiv:2604.27003 (abstract procedural memory transfers better than trajectories) is correctly flagged as a near-miss on M2>M3; the redaction design is a genuine tightening of it, and is the single most defensible novel element here.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline causal test is underpowered by the proposal's own arithmetic. Measurement and Noise Control states the memory x floor interaction - a difference of two paired differences - is detectable at ~6 points at n=500. Prediction 3 predicts breaks under M1 of ~50/500 = 10 points, cut by >=50% = a 5-point reduction, against an M0+Fh gain of '<1/3 of that' = <1.7 points. The predicted interaction is therefore ~3.3 points, roughly half the stated MDE. The single experiment that the proposal designates as 'the causal test' (Analysis 2) is thus specified to produce an effect it cannot resolve, and every arm downstream of it - M6, M7, and the entire division-of-labour comparison in Analysis 4, which compares M1+Fs and G1 against a 5-point M1+Fh benefit and asks whether they recover less than a third of it, i.e. resolving ~1.7-point differences - inherits that problem. The proposal is otherwise unusually rigorous about power, which makes this internally inconsistent rather than merely optimistic. Compounding it: the headline quantity is written as (breaks under M1 - breaks under M1+Fh) - (errors under M0 - errors under M0+Fh), which mixes a paired relative measure ('breaks', defined against M0) with an absolute one ('errors'), and never says whether breaks under M1+Fh are scored against M0 or M0+Fh; those two choices give different numbers and one of them makes the interaction partly definitional. Second-order but serious: even a clean positive interaction is confounded with error composition. M1 has more search-remediable errors available to fix than M0 by construction (that is what 'break' means), so a larger absolute floor benefit under M1 is the base-rate expectation, not evidence for a memory-specific mechanism; the comparison needs stratification on matched baseline error type or a relative-risk formulation, not raw absolute points. Third, prediction 6 - the claim the abstract calls 'sharp and risky' - is close to tautological. That a harness-enforced constraint outperforms the same constraint stated as text is the standing result of the instruction-following literature; M1+Fs is near-certain to lose, and G1 is a 400-rollout search over the instruction slot whose failure Risk 5 pre-emptively downgrades to 'inconclusive on enforcement-vs-discovery' if no verification language emerges. The prediction is thus arranged so that the interesting outcome is near-guaranteed and the uninteresting one is unreportable, which is the opposite of risk.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Re-derive the power for Analysis 2 as the primary endpoint and size n to it: either raise the paired test set (n~1200-1500 rather than 500, which the 40-node-hour budget can absorb by cutting the M3, M4 and M5 arms to a smaller subset), or select the test split enriched for instances where the precheck bank actually retrieves outcome-bearing near-neighbours, so the M1 break rate is 20-25% rather than 10% and a halving is a 10-12 point swing. State the interaction MDE and the predicted interaction in the same units in the same paragraph. (2) Fix the estimand: define breaks under every floor arm against a single fixed reference (M0, no floor), report the interaction as a ratio of break rates with a stratified analysis conditioning on M0 error type, and show the floor benefit is not explained by M1's richer supply of search-remediable errors. (3) Make prediction (iii) risky by giving the instruction slot its fair chance and by testing the other half of the division of labour: run GEPA (or a ReasoningBank-style rewriter) on the memory/demonstration slot at the same reflective budget, and run G1+Fh. 'Instruction search cannot repair a demonstration-slot pathology' is only a division-of-labour claim if the demonstration-slot search is shown to repair it. (4) Disentangle the mediator from the intervention. The title claims agents stop looking; the intervention that works requires them to cite. Add an arm that raises search depth without any justification requirement and with the sufficiency check applied only silently post hoc (M6 is close but keeps no sufficiency requirement at all), and an arm where memory is injected only after the agent has completed its own retrieval - if late injection removes the harm, the mechanism is 'never starts looking', not 'stops looking early', and the paper's central noun changes. (5) Pre-register the leakage audit threshold for M2 and state what leakage rate voids the redaction contrast, since procedural text in multi-hop QA ('look up the 1994 record holder, then their birthplace') encodes the answer path almost completely and a high leak rate makes M2 an outcome arm in disguise.
reviews.missing_baseline: A searched demonstration-slot repair: GEPA (or any reflective optimizer) applied to memory content itself - rewriting, filtering or abstracting the frozen bank - at the same 400-rollout budget and the same reflective access to shortcutting failures. The track's question is instructions versus demonstrations; the plan searches only the instruction slot (G1/G0) and pits it against a hand-written control-flow guard, so 'the repair belongs to the control flow' is asserted without ever testing whether it belongs to the demonstration slot. M2 is a hand-written demonstration-slot repair and is predicted to work, which makes the omission of its searched counterpart conspicuous: if a memory-slot optimizer matches M1+Fh, the correct conclusion is 'this is a demonstration-slot problem fixable in the demonstration slot', not 'prompt optimization cannot own it'. Also absent and cheap: G1+Fh (are instruction search and the floor additive or redundant?); a late-injection arm (memory revealed only after the agent's own retrieval completes), which is the strongest content-free competitor to the floor and costs no extra calls; and an abstention/'insufficient evidence' baseline, since converting a memory-induced wrong answer into a refusal is a live alternative repair that the fix/break table would score very differently.
reviews.preprint_collision: Above average for this kind of section and clearly done in good faith: it names one genuine partial collision (2505.16067) and concedes the phenomenon rather than claiming it, flags 2604.27003 as a near-miss on the M2/M3 contrast, states an explicit gap, and admits it could not sweep ICLR/NeurIPS 2026 portals. It also volunteers that an earlier draft carried a dozen unverifiable forward-dated IDs, which is honest but should make a reviewer check the surviving IDs. The check is nonetheless incomplete in exactly the region where this proposal's own mechanism lives. It searched the memory literature and not the stopping/sufficiency literature: nothing on sufficient-context and abstention in RAG (Joren et al., ICLR 2025 and successors), which already instruments the identical 'do the supporting spans appear in this episode's retrievals' binary and already reports models answering confidently without them; nothing on citation-grounded/verify-before-answer generation (Self-RAG, attribution-constrained decoding), which is what the evidence floor is; and nothing substantive on premature stopping in search/deep-research agents beyond a one-line dismissal of 'AgentStop-style early-exit papers' as the mirror image. That dismissal is too quick - efficiency-motivated early-exit work measures the exact endpoints proposed here (tool calls before answer, accuracy lost to stopping early) and several such papers report the accuracy cost of truncated search, which is prediction 1 in the other direction. No search is reported for the specific conjunction 'retrieved experience' + 'stopping/termination', which is the claim. So: no named preprint that I can point to makes this exact claim, but the check does not establish that, and its blind spot is not peripheral - it is the mediator and the intervention.
